takeaways: Fabric runs as one shared platform inside your tenant, so a single capacity is at once a billing object, a performance boundary and a blast radius.
Workspaces are the real unit of control, so every workspace needs a name, an owner, group-based roles and a lifecycle before sprawl sets in.
Security, labels and AI agents only protect what is configured at every layer, so review tenant settings, OneLake access paths and copied Microsoft 365 data early.
hook: Microsoft Fabric often appears in a tenant before anyone has planned its governance. This episode gives Microsoft 365 admins the platform view: how capacities, OneLake, workspaces, tenant settings, identity, labels and licensing fit together. It ends with a practical 30-day plan to put owners and guardrails in place before data and costs drift.
